question: What is this app?
answer:
This is a web app that holds a collection of prompts I wrote for creating multiple-choice questions with an AI chatbot. I have spent a lot of time writing questions this way, and these are the prompts I found most useful.

The app does not talk to the AI itself. It gives you the prompts, you paste them in, and you decide what to do with what comes back.

It is built for research participants, and general usage data are collected and followed up on in the closing interview.

question: What do I need to get started?
answer: Two things: your **participant code**, which the researcher assigned to you during the consent process, and access to an AI product such as ChatGPT, Gemini, or Copilot.

question: What is a participant code?
answer: Your participant code was assigned to you by the researcher during the consent process. If you do not have one, or have forgotten it, contact the researcher.

question: Do I need to install anything?
answer: No. Everything runs in your web browser. There is nothing to download and no account to create.

question: How long does a session take?
answer:
Expect roughly a minute per question if you are moving quickly, and several minutes per question if you are refining carefully.

The limiting factor is usually not how fast the AI responds. It is your own thinking about whether a question is appropriate for your students and good enough to keep.

question: What is training mode?
answer:
Training mode is a guided practice run of the app, used as part of the training module. It adds blue **Training tip** boxes explaining what each section does and what to do next.

It also includes a session timer that will alert you once you reach a certain point. That alert is part of the training module experience. If you are not working through the module right now, you can ignore it.

If you hide the tips and want them back, click **Show training tips** at the bottom of the page.

question: Can I use this app on my phone or tablet?
answer: Yes. The app works on all devices and adjusts to fit smaller screens. A desktop or laptop is more efficient, because you can keep the app and your AI product visible side by side instead of switching between two apps.

question: Do I need to be good with AI to use this?
answer:
No. These chatbots are designed to be easy to interact with. They respond in a natural, human-like way, so using one feels more like a conversation than like operating software. You mostly just talk to it.

There are a few things AI tends to do that cause frustration or poor results, but the prompts in this app are written to make it unlikely you will get steered too far off course.

question: What is a clipboard, and how do I copy and paste?
answer:
When you copy something, your computer holds it in a temporary space called the clipboard. It stays there until you copy something else. Pasting drops that text wherever your cursor is.

To paste:
• **Right-click** where you want the text and choose **Paste**
• **Windows/Chromebook:** Ctrl+V
• **Mac:** Command+V
• **Mobile:** Tap and hold in the text field, then tap **Paste**

When you click a **Copy** button in this app, nothing visible happens. That throws people off, but the prompt is on your clipboard. Switch to your AI, click in the message box, and paste.

question: What is the basic workflow, in one paragraph?
answer: You tell the app your course and topic, copy the starter prompt into your AI, and the AI returns a plan for the question set. You then work through questions one at a time: generate, look it over, refine the correct answer or the distractors if needed, and accept it. Every so often you can run an audit to see the shape of the whole set. When you are finished, you copy a final prompt that asks the AI to list everything cleanly.

question: Can I type my own instructions instead of using the buttons?
answer:
Definitely. There will be times you want to tell the chatbot something specific that no pre-made prompt covers.

When that happens, just talk to it the way you would talk to a person. Type out what you want and send it yourself. That is completely fine and expected. The prompts exist for the requests that come up over and over, not to limit what you can say.

question: How is this section organized?
answer:
Each entry below explains one button: what it does and when to use it. They are listed roughly in the order you will meet them.

One thing applies to all of them: clicking a prompt button copies text to your clipboard. Nothing is sent to your AI automatically. You paste it yourself, and you can edit it before you send it.

question: Explain the "Copy starter prompt" button
answer:
**What it does:** Copies the opening prompt that sets up your AI conversation. It passes along your course, topic, question count, and any extra notes, and sets the ground rules for how questions should be formatted and delivered one at a time.

**When to use it:** Once, at the start of every session, after filling in your context fields.

**What to expect back:** Not questions yet. The AI first replies with a table outlining the plan for the set.

question: Why is the "Copy starter prompt" button not working?
answer:
It stays dimmed until you have filled in both the Course and Topic fields.

That is because the starter prompt is built from the information you enter. Without those fields it has nothing to work with. Complete them and the button becomes available.

question: How do the sample question buttons work?
answer:
**Match Question Style**, **Create New Versions**, **Supplement Question Set**, and **Prepare Practice Questions** all work the same way. Each takes questions you already have and does something different with them.

**How to use any of them:**
1. Click the button to copy the prompt
2. Paste it into your AI. You will see the prompt ends with deliberately empty space at the bottom
3. Go find the questions you want to use, copy them, and paste them into that empty space
4. Send

**You do not need to clean up your questions first.** If there is stray numbering, leftover formatting, or extra text mixed in, paste it anyway. The AI will work around it. Tidying it up first is usually wasted effort.

question: Explain the "Match Question Style" button
answer:
**What it does:** Asks the AI to study questions you already have and match their characteristics as closely as possible without copying them.

**When to use it:** When you want new questions to resemble the voice, length, or difficulty of an existing set.

**How to use it:** Copy the prompt and paste it into your AI. The prompt ends with empty space. Copy your sample questions from wherever they live and paste them into that space, then send. No need to reformat or clean them up first.

question: Explain the "Create New Versions" button
answer:
**What it does:** Asks the AI to take questions you already have and write new versions on the same topics, keeping the concept and cognitive level but changing the wording, scenarios, and options enough to be meaningfully different.

**When to use it:** When you need a second form of an exam, a makeup version, or a fresh set for a repeat offering.

**How to use it:** Copy the prompt and paste it into your AI. The prompt ends with empty space. Copy your existing questions and paste them into that space, then send. No need to reformat or clean them up first.

question: Explain the "Supplement Question Set" button
answer:
**What it does:** Asks the AI to look at questions you already have and generate new ones on the same subject without overlapping in content. It infers the scope and level of your set, then broadens coverage around it.

**When to use it:** When you have a partial set and want to fill it out without duplicating what you already wrote.

**How to use it:** Copy the prompt and paste it into your AI. The prompt ends with empty space. Copy your existing questions and paste them into that space, then send. No need to reformat or clean them up first.

question: Explain the "Prepare Practice Questions" button
answer:
**What it does:** Asks the AI to take sample questions from an exam students will take and build practice questions around them, targeting the underlying concepts rather than narrowly rewriting the exam.

**When to use it:** When you want to give students practice material without teaching to the test.

**How to use it:** Copy the prompt and paste it into your AI. The prompt ends with empty space. Copy your exam questions and paste them into that space, then send. No need to reformat or clean them up first.

question: Explain the "Proceed to Making Questions" button
answer:
**What it does:** Moves you from setup into the main question-building phase.

**When to use it:** Once you have copied the starter prompt, sent it, and are satisfied with the plan the AI returned.

**If it will not respond:** It requires the earlier steps. Fill in the required context fields and copy the starter prompt first.

question: Explain the "Accept & Continue" button
answer:
**What it does:** Tells the AI the current question is acceptable, to add it to the working list, and to move on to the next one while keeping your parameters in place.

**When to use it:** Whenever a question is good enough to keep. This is the button you will press most often.

question: Explain the "Generate Alternatives" button
answer:
**What it does:** Asks for five replacement versions of the current question. One matches the same parameters but is meaningfully different, two approach the subtopic from different cognitive angles, and two address a different aspect of it. They come numbered, so you can reply with just the number you want.

**When to use it:** When a question is not wrong exactly, but you want options before committing.

question: Explain the "Refine Correct Answer" button
answer:
**What it does:** Asks the AI to rewrite the correct answer five different ways, each similar in length and complexity to the distractors. They come numbered.

**When to use it:** When the correct answer stands out from the other options, usually by being longer or more detailed. A test-wise student can spot an answer like that without knowing the content.

question: Explain the "Refine Distractors" button
answer:
**What it does:** Asks the AI to revise any original distractors that do not match the correct answer in length or complexity, then add ten more plausible options, presented as one numbered list of thirteen.

**When to use it:** When the wrong answers are too obviously wrong to tempt anyone. Instead of coaching the AI on how to write a good distractor, you ask for volume and pick the ones that would actually catch a student with incomplete understanding.

question: Explain the "Review Questions" button
answer:
**What it does:** Asks the AI to pause and display every question generated so far in a compact list, without revising any wording.

**When to use it:** Any time you lose track of what you have built, or want to look the set over before deciding what to do next.

question: Explain the "I'm done making questions" button
answer:
**What it does:** Moves you out of question-building and into finalizing.

**When to use it:** When you are satisfied with your set.

question: What are the audit buttons for?
answer:
The audit buttons ask the AI to stop and look at your whole set at once, rather than one question at a time. They catch patterns you cannot see while writing, such as a set that has quietly drifted toward one kind of question.

They are all optional.

question: Explain the "Topic Coverage Audit" button
answer:
**What it does:** Breaks your content area into subtopics, shows how many questions you have for each, and lists ten subtopics with no questions at all.

**When to use it:** When you want to see whether your set is drifting toward a few favorite subtopics, or when you need ideas for what to write next.

question: Explain the "Breadth Audit" button
answer:
**What it does:** Classifies each question as **Core**, the most common or first-line fact, or **Peripheral**, a less obvious but still clinically important area. It returns a table and suggests a peripheral angle for each core question.

**When to use it:** When you suspect your set is all low-hanging fruit. AI models tend to reach for the most obvious question on any topic.

question: Explain the "Question Type Audit" button
answer:
**What it does:** Sorts your questions by cognitive task, such as prioritization, delegation, assessment interpretation, interventions, patient teaching, pharmacology, ethical and legal, or procedures. It reports counts per category and suggests how to rebalance.

**When to use it:** When you want to be sure the set is not all interventions, or all pharmacology.

question: Explain the "Difficulty Audit" button
answer:
**What it does:** Classifies each question as Easy, Moderate, or Hard based on cognitive demand, stem complexity, and how subtle the distractors are, then shows the distribution.

**When to use it:** When you want a deliberate spread of difficulty rather than an accidental one.

question: Explain the "Bloom's Level Audit" button
answer:
**What it does:** Assigns each question a Bloom's taxonomy level, shows counts and percentages, and suggests how to cover underrepresented levels.

**When to use it:** When you want to check that a set is not entirely recall.

Keep in mind that a higher Bloom's level is not automatically better. Match the level to what you are trying to assess.

question: Explain the "Copy Final Prompt" button
answer:
**What it does:** Asks the AI to display every question you accepted, exactly as finalized, in a clean list with a short title, the stem, and options labeled A through D, correct answer first and bolded. Questions that were generated but never accepted are excluded.

**When to use it:** At the end of a session, when you want one tidy copy of everything you built.

question: Explain the "End session" button
answer:
**What it does:** Closes out your session and submits your session data. If you want to share the AI's final compiled question set, paste it into the optional box first. A confirmation dialog appears, and ending clears this browser's stored session data.

**When to use it:** When you are finished working.

question: Explain the "Reset session" button
answer:
**What it does:** Clears all progress for the current browser session and returns you to the sign-in screen. Anything already submitted is retained; the reset only clears what is stored in this browser.

**When to use it:** When you want a clean start, or something has gotten into a confusing state.

question: Explain the "Show training tips" button
answer: **What it does:** Brings back the blue training tip boxes if you have hidden them. It sits at the bottom of the page.

question: How do I copy and paste prompts?
answer:
Click any **Copy** button in the app. The prompt text goes to your clipboard. Nothing visible happens when you click, which surprises people, but it worked.

Then switch to your AI product, click in the message box, and paste:
• **Right-click** and choose **Paste**
• **Windows/Chromebook:** Ctrl+V
• **Mac:** Command+V
• **Mobile:** Tap and hold in the text field, then tap **Paste**

question: Do I have to use the buttons in order?
answer: No. The buttons are arranged roughly in the order they tend to be useful, but you can use whichever ones you want and skip the rest.

question: Can I edit a prompt before sending it?
answer: Yes. Once a prompt is on your clipboard it is just text. Paste it into your AI, change anything you like, and send it.

question: Can I talk to the AI directly during a session?
answer:
Yes, at any point. The most common example is steering the plan at the beginning, where you might simply type something like "these two subtopics are too advanced for this course."

The buttons save you time on the prompts that come up repeatedly. They are not a limit on what you can say.

question: Can I see the full text of a prompt before I send it?
answer: Yes. On any device, click the small arrow next to a button to expand it and read the text. On desktop you also have the sidebar, where the full prompt appears when you copy it.

question: Do I have to write my questions one at a time?
answer:
The app is designed around building one set at a time, with the AI producing questions one by one so you can react to each. In practice this produces a more coherent set than asking for ten at once.

That said, if you want to move quickly through the opening section to get to the question-building phase, that is completely acceptable.

question: What if the AI gives me all the questions at once instead of one at a time?
answer: The starter prompt asks it to pause after each question, but models do not always comply. If it hands you a whole set, just reply and ask it to go back to one at a time.

question: How many questions should I make?
answer: The default is ten, which most AI products handle comfortably in a single conversation. You can set it higher or lower. Longer sets sometimes drift in quality toward the end, so if you need forty questions, consider several shorter sessions.

question: How do I end my session?
answer: Click **End session**. If you want to share the AI's final compiled question set, paste it into the optional box first. A confirmation dialog appears. Ending clears this browser's stored session data and submits your session.

question: Does the app save my questions?
answer: The app is not a question bank. Your questions live in your AI conversation. If you want to keep them, use **Copy Final Prompt** at the end and save the AI's response somewhere of your own.

question: What happens if I close my AI conversation?
answer: The AI loses the context of your session, including your parameters and the questions built so far. Start a new conversation and paste the starter prompt again. If you have questions you want to keep working from, paste them in as samples.

question: How can I use the questions made by this app?
answer:
The obvious uses:
• Unit exams, midterms, and finals
• Quizzes, including low-stakes weekly ones
• Practice tests and exam review sets
• Homework or pre-class comprehension checks
• Building a reusable question bank over time

There are also some less obvious uses, covered in the entries below.

question: Can I use these questions for in-class activities?
answer: Yes. A single well-built question works as a class opener, a mid-lecture check, or an exit ticket. Retrieval practice works even when nothing is graded, so a question answered out loud or on a polling tool still helps.

question: Can I use the wrong answers as a teaching tool?
answer: This is one of the best uses and the most commonly missed. A good distractor represents a specific misconception. Putting a question on screen and asking students to explain **why** each wrong option is wrong turns the distractors into the lesson.

question: Can I have students critique the questions?
answer: Yes. Give students a question and ask them to evaluate it. Working out why an option gives itself away, or why a stem is ambiguous, forces engagement with the content and builds test-taking insight that transfers to the NCLEX.

question: Can I use these for simulation or clinical debriefing?
answer: Yes. Generate a short set tied to the scenario your students just completed and use them to anchor the debrief. A concrete question about a decision point often starts a better discussion than an open invitation to reflect.

question: Can I use these to create makeup or alternate exam versions?
answer: Yes. The **Create New Versions** prompt is built for this: same concepts and cognitive level, different wording, scenarios, and options.

question: Can I use these for remediation with a struggling student?
answer: Yes. Generate a small targeted set on the concepts a student is missing and use them as a self-check before a meeting. It gives you both something concrete to work from.

question: Can I give questions to students to quiz themselves?
answer: Yes. Students rarely practice retrieval on their own unless handed something structured. A short self-quiz with answers is a low-effort way to give them that.

question: Can I use these to find gaps in my own teaching?
answer: Run a **Topic Coverage Audit** or **Question Type Audit** on a set built from your course material. The gaps it reports often mirror gaps in what you actually emphasized.

question: Can I use these with colleagues?
answer: Yes. Bringing a generated set to a peer review conversation gives colleagues something concrete to react to. It is usually easier to critique a draft question than to write one from scratch in a meeting.

question: Should I use these questions exactly as the AI writes them?
answer: No. The AI supplies speed and range; you supply the judgment about your content and your students. Anything you would not have written yourself is worth a second look before it reaches a student.

question: Do I need to check the questions for accuracy?
answer: Yes, always. AI products can produce content that is confidently stated and wrong. Treat every question as a draft from a fast but unreliable colleague.

question: Which AI product should I use?
answer: Any of the major ones will work. Use whichever your institution provides or whichever you already have. The app provides one shared set of prompts. You do not need to select a product in the app.

question: Do I need a paid AI subscription?
answer:
No. The free tier of any major AI product is enough for this workflow, though free tiers often limit how many messages you can send per day.

Paid versions generally give you access to more capable models, longer conversations, and higher usage limits, which can mean more nuanced responses. Helpful, but not required.

question: Which model or mode should I choose?
answer: The default model is capable of doing this. If your product offers a deeper thinking or reasoning mode, in my opinion it is worth the slightly slower responses, but that is a personal preference rather than a requirement. If the options are confusing, use the default.

question: Do I need to confirm an AI mode?
answer: No. There is no product-selection or mode-confirmation step. Start with your question context and paste the prompts into the chatbot you choose.

question: Can I use a different AI product?
answer: Yes. The app does not require you to choose an AI product. Copy any prompt and paste it into whichever chatbot you use, including products other than ChatGPT, Gemini, or Copilot. Responses may vary by product.

question: Can I switch AI products during a session?
answer: Yes. The app uses the same prompts for every chatbot, so you can switch products without resetting the app. However, chatbots do not automatically share conversation history. You may need to paste your context and previously accepted questions into the new conversation.

question: Can I upload my course documents to the AI?
answer: That depends on your AI product and on your institution's policies. If you do, be careful not to upload anything containing student information or other protected material.

question: Is it safe to put my course content into an AI?
answer: Follow your institution's guidance on generative AI. As a general rule, avoid entering student names, grades, protected health information, proprietary test banks, or anything you would not want stored on an outside server.

question: What data are collected?
answer:
The version you are using records:
• Your participant code
• Whether you are in standard mode or training mode
• The course, topic, question count, and any extra instructions you provided
• Which prompts you copied and when
• Any final question set you choose to paste into the optional sharing box
• Any text or audio feedback you choose to provide
• Session activity and timing information

The app does **not** record your AI conversation itself. It only sees what you paste into it.

There is also an open version of this app, not connected to the study, which collects far less.

question: Are my data stored on this device?
answer: The app keeps a recovery copy of your current work and participant code in this browser. It also saves confirmed progress to the secure study database. Automatic return lasts up to 24 hours and your code is checked with the server when the page opens. On a shared device, use Log out when finished; this clears this app’s saved work and previous settings from the browser. A recovery copy awaiting confirmation is retained so a failed request can be retried.

question: What will my data be used for?
answer: Your session data will be used as part of a doctoral dissertation study examining how nursing faculty experience using AI-assisted question-generation tools. Any final AI response you choose to share is used as a reference point for the follow-up interview. It is not graded or evaluated on its own.

question: Will my responses be kept confidential?
answer: Yes. Data are identified by participant code rather than by name in the app workflow. The researcher follows all protocols approved by the Institutional Review Board to protect confidentiality.

question: Do I have to share my final question set?
answer: No. The sharing box is entirely optional and has no effect on your compensation. It exists only so that, if you want to discuss something specific in the closing interview, it is easy to reference.

question: What should I avoid pasting into the app?
answer: Please do not paste anything containing restricted, protected, or confidential information about yourself, your institution, or any other individual. That includes student names, grades, and anything drawn from protected records.

question: The app is not loading or looks broken.
answer:
Try these steps:
1. Refresh the page
2. Check that you have a stable internet connection
3. Try a different browser, such as Chrome or Edge
4. Clear your browser cache and try again

If the problem persists, contact the researcher.

question: A button is not responding when I click it.
answer: Some buttons require earlier steps to be completed. For example, **Proceed to Making Questions** requires you to fill in the required context fields and copy the starter prompt. If a button still does not respond, refresh the page and try again.

question: The prompts do not seem to be loading.
answer: The app loads prompt text from a remote server when it starts. If your connection is slow or unavailable, it can fall back to built-in prompts. If you see an error message, try refreshing the page.

question: Nothing pasted when I hit Ctrl+V.
answer: Some browsers block clipboard access until you interact with the page. Click somewhere on the page and try the copy button again. If that fails, expand the prompt with the small arrow next to the button and select the text manually.

question: I pasted a prompt but the AI did not respond well.
answer: AI responses vary. Try pasting the same prompt again, use a different prompt button, or type your own instructions directly into the conversation.

question: The AI ignored my instructions or drifted off topic.
answer: This happens, especially in long conversations. Restate your parameters in a sentence or two. If it keeps drifting, start a fresh conversation with the starter prompt and paste in any questions you want to keep.

question: The AI keeps writing the same kind of question over and over.
answer: This is a known tendency, and it is what the audit buttons are for. Run a **Question Type Audit** or **Breadth Audit**, see what is overrepresented, and tell the AI what you want next.

question: The AI's questions are too easy, or too hard.
answer: Tell it directly. You can also run the **Difficulty Audit** or **Bloom's Level Audit** to see the distribution, then ask for more questions at the level you are missing.

question: The correct answer is always the longest option.
answer: One of the most common AI patterns. Use **Refine Correct Answer**, which asks for versions matching the distractors in length and complexity, and pick one that blends in.

question: I accidentally closed the browser. Are my progress and work lost?
answer: Sign in again with the same participant code. The app checks the study database for your saved session and uses any recovery copy in this browser to retry unconfirmed saves. Work that was never saved to the server can be lost if you clear browser data or use a different device. Before closing, wait for a successful save or submission message. An unuploaded audio recording is held in memory; download it before closing the page.

question: How do I reset and start over?
answer: Click **Reset session** at the top of the page. This clears all progress for your current browser session and returns you to the sign-in screen. Any data already submitted are retained.

question: Can I run multiple sessions?
answer: Yes. Each time you sign in with your participant code, a new session can be created. Starting a new session does not affect earlier sessions already submitted.

question: My session timer ran out. What now?
answer: The timer appears in training mode as part of the guided practice. Reaching the end of it is not a failure and does not stop you from continuing. Follow whatever instructions the module gives you at that point.

question: Something is broken and none of this helped.
answer: Use the **Report issue** option if it is available to you, or email the researcher at tjin@crimson.ua.edu. A short description of what you clicked and what happened is enough.

question: Who is eligible to participate in the study?
answer: The study is intended for eligible nursing faculty as described in the study materials. If you want to know whether you qualify, use the study-information or recruitment link provided on the start page.

question: What happens after I complete my session?
answer: The researcher may review the submitted data and use them as a reference point for the follow-up interview. The interview focuses on your experience using the tool: what worked, what did not, and your overall impressions.

question: Do I need to produce a certain number of questions?
answer: No. There is no required number. The study is about your experience with the process, not the quantity of output.

question: Do I have to use the app?
answer: No. The practice period is voluntary. Choosing not to use the tool is still meaningful to the study, and the researcher is just as interested in hearing why.

question: Can I stop participating?
answer: Participation is voluntary. If you have questions about stopping or withdrawing, contact the researcher using the study contact information provided in the study materials.

question: Will I be judged on the questions I write?
answer: No. Nothing you produce is graded or evaluated for quality. The study is interested in your experience of the process, not in the output.

question: What if I did not like using the app?
answer: That is a legitimate and useful finding, and the researcher genuinely wants to hear it. Critical feedback is at least as valuable as positive feedback.

question: Who do I contact if I have questions about the study or the app?
answer: Contact the researcher, Taemin Jin, at tjin@crimson.ua.edu.
